description: Issue #839: when a program contains BOTH kinds of declaration-slot collision, the first one in SOURCE ORDER halts it. Here a duplicate `tally` on line 4 precedes a built-in `define forward` on line 7, and the duplicate is what is reported — the run stops there, so the later `ol-reserved-word` is never produced. This is the ordering property, deliberately separated from the *priority* property (`ol-reserved-word` beats `ol-duplicate-definition` when ONE name is both), which is a check-stage concern because `check()` reports every finding while `execute()` stops at the first. The mirror program — the `define forward` block first, then the duplicated `tally` — reports `ol-reserved-word` at the built-in declaration instead and never reaches the duplicate; it is pinned as a unit test (`execute-declaration-slots.test.mjs`, "the first collision in source order halts the run, whichever code it carries") rather than as a second fixture, since the two differ only in block order. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why only one report survives and it reads `stage: "semantic"`.
